newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium 1995 current account surplus 312 bln Bfr.
newsitem.headline: Belgium 1995 current account surplus 312 bln Bfr.

text.p: The Belgian National Bank (BNB) said on Friday Belgium's current account surplus was 312 billion Belgian francs in 1995, or 76 percent of the total of the Belgo-Luxembourg economic union (BLEU).
It is the first time separate figures were given for the Belgian current account. Previously, the two countries' current account data were reported as one.
The current account is the measure of Belgium's financial position vis-a-vis the rest of the world, measuring both trade in goods, services and investments.
Belgium has always claimed it accounted for the bulk of the BLEU's surplus and therefore for the strength of the Belgian and Luxembourg francs, which are linked.

The BNB said Belgium had a 293 billion franc trade surplus, an eight billion franc surplus on services, and a 119 billion franc surplus from investment and other revenues. It had a 108 billion franc deficit on other overseas transfers. -- Nick Antonovics, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6817
